display.purpose: Hero headlines, section H1s, and stat numbers users should feel oriented or proud of (kcal targets, streak counts, BMI).

title.purpose: Card/component titles nested under a headline.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, stat captions, section tags — uppercase wide-tracked.

shadows.name: hero-float
shadows.purpose: Reserved for the single most important visual artifact on a page (e.g. landing-page AI-scan preview card).

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus color shift on buttons, links, nav items.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action button; solid sage, white text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: #426449; color: #ffffff; border: none; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #35523b; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #426449; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.6; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Bordered white button for secondary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: #ffffff; color: #1c1b1b; border: 1px solid #eae7e7; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: #426449; color: #426449; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #426449; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Default content container: white surface, hairline border, no shadow.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #eae7e7; border-radius: 12px; padding: 24px; } .ds-card-eyebrow { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8a8787; margin: 0; } .ds-card-stat { font-family: 'Shippori Mincho', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 28px; color: #1c1b1b; margin: 8px 0 0; } .ds-card-stat span { font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: #5f5d5d; font-weight: 400; margin-left: 4px; }

components.name: Pill (Sage)
components.description: Default informational pill/badge — eyebrow tags, suggestion chips.
components.html: 14 Hari Streak

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard form field with sage focus ring.
components.css: .ds-field { width: 100%; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #eae7e7; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 14px; font-size: 14px; color: #1c1b1b; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, box-shadow 0.15s ease; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: #8a8787; } .ds-field:focus { border-color: #426449; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(66, 100, 73, 0.2); }

components.name: Progress Ring
components.description: Signature conic-gradient progress indicator; always single-hue sage regardless of value.

narrative.overview: Raifu reads like the entrance to a calm Japanese inn: soft sage and warm cream tones, generous whitespace, a serif display face for moments that matter, and quiet borders instead of shadows doing the organizing. Nothing shouts. Numbers (calorie targets, macros, streak counts) get the display serif treatment so they feel like considered facts, not alarms — the opposite of a fitness app's urgency dashboard. The system explicitly rejects loud fitness-app energy: no countdown timers, no red/orange danger-zone bars, no gamified urgency cues. Progress (rings, bars) always renders in the single sage accent, never a traffic-light palette. This mirrors the product's "no guilt tracking" principle from PRODUCT.md — the visual system must never make a number look like a failure.
keyCharacteristics: Sage-and-cream palette with a single accent color used sparingly (never a full-saturation 'brand wash')
Serif display type (Shippori Mincho) for headlines and hero numbers; Inter for everything functional
Flat-by-default surfaces bordered in a near-invisible hairline, not shadowed
Occasional Japanese script (楽, 腹八分目) as philosophy marks, not a translation layer
Rounded, soft-edged geometry throughout — no sharp corners, no aggressive shapes

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Sage is the only color that carries meaning (selected, active, progress, success). No second accent color exists; do not introduce blue links, red errors, or orange warnings without a documented reason.

rules.name: The No Alarm Rule
rules.body: Never use red, orange, or amber to represent calorie overage, missed streaks, or incomplete goals. A missed day or exceeded target renders in the same neutral/sage vocabulary as everything else.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Facts Rule
rules.body: Any number the user should feel proud of or oriented by (kcal target, streak count, BMI, macro grams) renders in the serif display font with tabular-nums, never in the body sans.

rules.name: The Flat-Except-One Rule
rules.body: A page gets at most one shadowed 'hero' element. Every other surface stays flat and relies on border/tone for separation.

dos: Do use the serif display face with tabular-nums for any number the user should feel oriented or proud of (targets, totals, streak counts, BMI).
Do separate surfaces with the border-line hairline or a tonal background shift before reaching for a shadow.
Do keep all progress indicators (rings, bars) in the single sage accent regardless of value.
Do use the uppercase, wide-tracked Eyebrow label style for section tags and stat captions.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color (blue, purple, teal) for links, selection, or emphasis — sage is the only accent.
Don't use red/orange/amber to signal exceeded calories, missed streaks, or incomplete goals — this breaks the no-guilt product principle.
Don't add drop shadows to ordinary cards or panels; reserve the single soft shadow for one hero artifact per page at most.
Don't introduce sharp corners, dense data-table spacing, or countdown-timer urgency patterns — they read as generic fitness-app energy, which this system explicitly rejects.
